implementation_notes: The Scala realization is an immutable wrapper: final case class Traced[T](payload: T, hops: Vector[Hop] = Vector.empty), each component publishing Traced(payload, hops :+ Hop(name, Instant.now())). Vector append is effectively constant time with structural sharing, so copying an envelope with a long history is cheap, and the classic mutable header list disappears in favour of value semantics; actor systems (Akka/Pekko) already pass immutable messages, which makes an envelope the natural carrier. At the transport boundary the list is serialized into the header (kafka-clients ProducerRecord#headers or a framework history header).
pitfalls: Case-class equality compares the entire hop list, so equals/hashCode (and pattern matches on envelopes) become expensive with long histories - compare payload ids or tag the envelope.
Per-hop cost still adds up on hot paths even with structural sharing; cap the vector and drop the oldest entries rather than growing it without bound.
Mixing mutable JVM collections (java.util.ArrayList) into the case class breaks the value semantics the idiom depends on: copies would share the list and branches would collide.
